title: U.S. House · Georgia's 3rd Congressional District
area: West-central Georgia, including Carrollton, Newnan, and Fayetteville.

context.text: Incumbent Brian Jack (R), first elected in 2024 and a former senior advisor on Donald Trump's presidential campaigns, advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Maura Keller won the Democratic primary over George Melville Johnson.

candidates.name: Brian Jack
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District (since 2025)

summary.text: Brian Jack is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. Before Congress he was a senior advisor for Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and an advisor for Trump's 2016 campaign, serving as national delegate management director ahead of the 2016 Republican National Convention.

background.text: Born in Georgia; earned a bachelor's degree from Pepperdine University in 2010; worked as a political analyst.
Served as a senior advisor for Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and as an advisor for his 2016 campaign, including as the campaign's national delegate management director.

priorities.text: Lists "Secure our Border, End Illegal Immigration and Stop Crime" as a top campaign priority, saying he will work to finish the border wall and deport people in the country illegally who commit crimes.
Lists "Fix the Economy, Cut Taxes and Unleash American Energy," saying he will work to lower taxes, cut spending, and increase U.S. oil and natural gas production.
Lists "End the Weaponization of Justice" as a priority, saying he will work against what he describes as politically motivated use of the justice system.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he will work to finish the border wall, fund ICE and border patrol, and deport people in the country illegally who have committed crimes; his office also highlighted co-sponsoring the Laken Riley Act, which requires DHS to detain certain unauthorized immigrants arrested for theft-related offenses.
positions.quote: In Congress, I will lead the fight to end Biden’s border invasion and put America First once again - completing the job President Trump and I began in 2016. That means finishing the border wall, funding for ICE and border patrol, deporting criminal illegals, and reforming our immigration laws to prioritize the prosperity of working class Americans.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Delivering on Government Efficiency, Federal Law Enforcement, and Government Operations subcommittees), the Committee on Rules, and the Committee on Small Business in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Co-sponsored the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29/S. 5), which requires DHS to detain certain unauthorized immigrants arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting; it was the first bill to pass the House in the 119th Congress and was signed into law.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities above are drawn from Jack's campaign website (still current on the 2026 cycle site) and an official House press release; no additional issue statements were found on his official House issues subpages (Economy, Education, Energy, Health, Veterans), which had no body text loaded.

candidates.name: Maura Keller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over George Melville Johnson.

summary.text: Maura Keller is a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District, campaigning on raising the minimum wage and economic opportunity for the district.

background.text: Born in South Weymouth, Massachusetts; has lived in Fayetteville, Georgia for about 30 years.

Enlisted in the U.S. Army in 1978, rose through the ranks, was commissioned as an officer, and retired as a lieutenant colonel after 26 years of service; later worked as a senior consultant on military personnel and readiness for the Department of Defense.
Earned a degree in Radiologic Sciences (Nuclear Medicine Technology) and worked at the Atlanta VA supporting veterans; received the General Douglas MacArthur Leadership Award.

priorities.text: Says a fairer economic future for the district must start with raising the minimum wage.
priorities.quote: I'm committed to creating real opportunities for everyone in District 3. A fairer economic future is the foundation of all my positions, and we must start by raising the minimum wage.

positions.summary: Says Georgia's livable wage should be at least $22/hour, and criticizes the district's past representatives for votes to keep the federal minimum at $7.25/hour.
